content.comment_body: After switching to a new Windows 11 laptop and replacing my desktop computer, I've lost previous installations of [product_name] ([version_no] initially and upgraded to [version_no]). Tried installing from the original CD, intending to run the upgrade afterwards. During Windows setup, I received an error message about the application quitting unexpectedly due to a Java InvocationTargetException. It seems this may be related to recent advice against installing Java on modern computers. Can someone suggest a workaround to get [product_name] working? I need to modify logic on an active system. Also, I can't find a way to reach anyone on the Help Desk by phone or online.

Welcome to the forum. The old software ([version_no]) isn't compatible with Windows 11. I'm unfamiliar with [product_name] [version_no]; this could be a typo and you might mean the current [version_no]. You can't install the upgrade to [version_no] if you only have an old installation medium as a full version. Check this FAQ for instructions on installing a downloaded upgrade for [product_name] with or without an existing installation.

Try installing on a different computer running an older operating system, then copy all contents of the installation directory (where [product_name] is installed, typically in Program Files) to the new computer. It's better to use a version that includes Java Runtime (JRE). You can create a desktop shortcut, etc. This method allows you to maintain several versions (with different directory names) on a memory stick and copy whichever is needed to your working machine. So far, subdirectory paths appear relative, so the main installation directory name shouldn't matter.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face significant compatibility problems when installing older versions of [product_name] on modern operating systems like Windows 11. One user encounters a Java-related error preventing installation, which reflects challenges with outdated dependencies and limited legacy support. The inability to contact customer support directly increases user frustration and reveals gaps in available support channels.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to be backward compatible with current Windows operating systems, straightforward upgrade procedures, and easily accessible technical support.
